articles.title: I got tired of eye-stinging campfire smoke, so I tested smokeless fire pits to find the best
articles.summary: We put half a dozen backyard smokeless fire pits – from Solo Stove, Breeo, BioLite and more – to the test. A campfire in your backyard seems like a nice idea – until you try one and end up shifting chairs every 30 seconds to escape the eye-searing smoke.
body: New models by Cuisinart, Breeo, Solo Stove and others help you meet all of those objectives with one product.

The reduced smoke comes from the clever double-wall construction. Air intake holes at the base draw cool air between the walls, which becomes superheated and spews out holes on the top, helping to burn uncombusted particulates and reducing visible smoke. The result is a fire that burns hotter and smokes less.

For our initial backyard smokeless fire pit testing at the Filter US (a part of the Guardian US newsroom), I reviewed six models, setting them all up in my driveway at the same time. I cooked burgers and steaks, checked the smoke levels and heat and tested how long each one lasted. After a month of testing, one clear winner stood out among several other smokeless options.
As I raced around my driveway, keeping all of my little fires burning like a wildman, cooking steaks and measuring the temp and smoke levels, one fire pit stood out in the crowd.
points: We put half a dozen backyard smokeless fire pits – from Solo Stove, Breeo, BioLite and more – to the test.

articles.title: What happens to your pets when you die?
articles.summary: Without a proper plan – whether in a trust or will – your beloved companion could face an animal shelter or worse. The idea of making a will may be uncomfortable, but routine. Ensuring that your family and estate is taken care of is a kindness.
body: Sometimes, “somebody wants to set up a trust with substantial money in it”, he said. But more typically, the client wants to ensure “the right person” gets the dog or cat – but has no idea how best to do it.
As the person in charge of your pet’s livelihood, you can (and should) try to get something on paper that makes sense.

“Pets rely entirely on human care. Without a plan, they face stress, shelter, surrender or unnecessary euthanasia during an already chaotic time,” said Peter Klein, the founder of the therapy referral website Seek a Psych and a London-based cognitive behavioral therapist in private practice.

According to a report from Best Friends Animal Society, a non-profit advocacy group working to achieve no-kill statuses for shelters around the United States, 12.4% of the 4.74 million cats and dogs that entered the shelter system in 2025 ended up there due to owner illness or death.
points: Without a proper plan – whether in a trust or will – your beloved companion could face an animal shelter or worse.

articles.title: Privileged and proud: how nepo babies took fashion month by storm
articles.summary: From commanding the catwalks to acting as plus-ones for their famous parents, celebrity kids are bang on trend. Knee-length skirts and bras worn as tops were two of the main takeaways from fashion month, which wrapped up this week. But the biggest trend had nothing to do with clothing.
body: John Travolta’s daughter, Ella Bleu, 26, made her Paris catwalk debut at Miu Miu. Apple Martin, 22, the daughter of Chris Martin and Gwyneth Paltrow, walked the Chloé show.

Meanwhile, the Vogue World event in Milan featured the Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli’s son Matteo, 29, Nick and Susie Cave’s son Earl, 26, Ava Phillippe, 27, the daughter of the actors Reese Witherspoon and Ryan Phillippe, and many more nepo babies in attendance.
Mark Borkowski, a PR consultant, described the nepo baby phenomenon as “a wonderful cocktail of youth, nostalgia and inherited glamour”.

Fran Hoepfner, the author of The Field Guide to Nepo Babies, said it was vital that a nepo had both a family connection and a direct or adjacent industry connection. “Simply having rich parents does not automatically make someone a nepo baby,” she said. “It just makes you lucky.”

articles.title: I hitchhiked from Sydney to Perth, and found comfort in the company of strangers
articles.summary: The lost practice of hitchhiking is a subculture, an art, and a way of travel that satisfies wanderlust like no other trip. Plus, it costs nothing. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. I’m alone, hunched over by a dusty road junction, and feeling the bite of the morning sun.
body: Most drivers who pass wave or give me a thumbs up. One gives me the finger. There isn’t much traffic. Someone tosses a water bottle out their window at me.

Just as I start to catastrophise in the dust, a four-wheel-drive quietly pulls off the road and comes to a stop behind me. I hoist my backpack around my shoulder, run over and jump in the passenger seat, thanking the driver profusely.

One of my stranger interests is hitchhiking. I’m drawn to the idea of abandoning control and finding comfort in a stranger’s company. It’s a subculture, an art, and a way of travel that satisfies wanderlust like no other trip. Plus, it costs nothing.

Once a popular way to travel in the 70s and 80s, these days it’s pretty rare to see a hitchhiker on the side of Australian roads. For starters, its reputation was overwhelmingly tarnished by its association with serial killer Ivan Milat, who murdered several hitchhikers in the early 90s. Australia is also one of the few countries in the world that make it legally fraught to hitchhike, with laws explicitly naming hitchhiking as an offence, though legislation differs between state and territories.
points: The lost practice of hitchhiking is a subculture, an art, and a way of travel that satisfies wanderlust like no other trip.

articles.title: Carnegie Hall’s Opening Night Gala Spotlighted the Power of Music
articles.summary: When the first orange-tinged leaves appear in Central Park, New Yorkers knows the Carnegie Hall fall season is just around the corner, too. On Thursday evening, the historic venue opened its doors to mark the start of its autumn program with a performance by the Berliner Philharmoniker.
body: Led by chief conductor Kirill Petrenko and featuring star tenor Jonas Kaufmann, the night’s show under the Hall’s gilded ceilings and boxes was an international display of talent. In the heart of midtown Manhattan, the German orchestra performed a program of Italian music spanning Verdi, Leoncavallo, and Respighi, among others. A raucous standing ovation—and surprise brass musicians emerging from the wings—proved no translator was needed to manage the combination of different cultures at play, as they were all united by the rousing emotion of the opera.

“It was beautiful,” Constance Wu, a longtime classical music enthusiast, told Vogue. “It was a very pastoral, woodland-type of program, which is a wonderful thing to listen to as summer turns to fall. It was a cool, dusky vibe, and the sound was incredible.”

After the performance, the celebrations continued at Cipriani 42nd Street for the event’s annual gala. With a celestial ‘Where the Stars Align’ theme, guests including designer Prabal Gurung, Peter Sarsgaard, Doris Wong, Jessica Joffe, Lena Hall, and Eletra Wiedemann were surrounded by vibrant sunflowers and flickering candlelight under the venue’s soaring columns.
points: When the first orange-tinged leaves appear in Central Park, New Yorkers knows the Carnegie Hall fall season is just around the corner, too.

articles.title: At The Albies, Amal and George Clooney Make Sure the Real-Life Heroes Take Center Stage
articles.summary: As one would imagine, Amal and George Clooney certainly have no issue pulling a crowd. As such, the host table placement at their fifth annual foundation gala, The Albies, did not disappoint.
body: On George’s left sat his longtime co-stars and friends Laura Dern and Brad Pitt. On the actor’s right, rapper and activist Vic Mensa and Downton Abbey’s Lord Grantham himself, Hugh Bonneville. With the inimitable couple separated only by the table’s elaborate edible display of Italian delicacies, Amal, draped in a gilded off-the-shoulder sequin gown by Gucci, was shoulder-to-shoulder with Vogue’s Anna Wintour, musician Jackson Browne, and actress Emma Thompson.

Still, even in a room bursting with headline-worthy names, the Clooneys ensured the spotlight shone brightest on the evening’s honorees: Kyrgyz journalists Bolot Temirov and Makhabat Tazhibek Kyzy, Malawian girls’ rights activist Vanessa Mwangala, American photojournalist Lynsey Addario, Congolese NGO Justice Plus, and Microsoft Vice Chair and President Brad Smith.

When it came to choosing this year’s award recipients, George remarked, “You have to look at things that are going on in the news. We’re looking for people that are shining a light on [an issue], can help put a protective shield over someone, or prevent them from being thrown in jail or killed.”

articles.title: How Milan Became Home to Europe's Best Cocktail Bar
articles.summary: One Milanese cocktail spot was just named the second-best bar in the world—but Milan has a long history as one of Europe's best drinking cities.
body: The World's 50 Best Bars for 2026 have just been revealed, and Milan has plenty to celebrate. Not only did Moebius Milano take second place in the global ranking, but it was also crowned the best bar in Europe. And, if that weren't enough, the awards ceremony itself took place in Milan on Wednesday, October 7, marking the first time the event has been hosted in Italy.

For a city that has always taken its aperitivo seriously, it's quite an achievement. Milan might be better known internationally for its fashion houses and design scene, but anyone who has spent an evening wandering around its neighborhoods will know that going out for a drink is practically part of a local's daily routine. And while the tradition of meeting friends for a pre-dinner spritz or negroni is hardly new, Milan's cocktail scene has evolved considerably in recent years, with a growing number of bars pushing the boundaries of what a night out in the city can look like.
points: One Milanese cocktail spot was just named the second-best bar in the world—but Milan has a long history as one of Europe's best drinking cities.

articles.title: BA’s Best Bolognese
articles.summary: Tender ground beef, savory pancetta, and a splash of white wine make this slow-simmered Bolognese worth the wait.
body: “It’s meat gravy.” That’s how recipe developer Andy Baraghani describes his Bolognese sauce, and he means it in the best possible way. This is a rich, deeply savory ragù that puts beef and pancetta front and center, with just enough tomato paste to bring it all together. No canned tomatoes, no laundry list of herbs, no unnecessary fuss.

The supporting cast matters too: Onion, carrot, and celery are chopped so finely they practically disappear into the sauce. White wine brightens without dominating the flavors, whole milk adds richness while helping tenderize the beef, and a pinch of nutmeg adds subtle warmth. The result is aromatic and flavorful without being heavy-handed.

You’ll need about three hours from start to finish, but most of that time is hands-off. Serve the meat sauce with fresh pasta like wide tagliatelle or pappardelle noodles, or dried rigatoni, which catches the meaty Bolognese in its ridges. It also freezes beautifully, so another pasta night is already halfway done.
points: Tender ground beef, savory pancetta, and a splash of white wine make this slow-simmered Bolognese worth the wait.
